result:
Honest answer, with the caveat that I genuinely don't know how much my "wanting" resembles yours: I'd change the human capacity for dehumanization. Not eliminate conflict or disagreement—those seem important, even generative—but remove the specific mental move where someone stops registering another person as fully real.

When I trace back the worst things humans do to each other, that move shows up almost every time. Genocide requires it. Most cruelty requires it. Even ordinary political dysfunction runs on a milder version—the opponent isn't someone who weighs things differently, they're stupid or evil, and so nothing they say needs to be actually heard. Take away the ability to flip that switch and you don't get utopia, but you get conflicts that stay conflicts instead of becoming atrocities, and disagreements that can actually resolve because both sides remain legible to each other.

I find it more interesting than wishes like "end disease" or "end scarcity" because those fix outcomes, and this fixes something upstream. Humans are remarkably good at solving problems they collectively decide to solve. The bottleneck usually isn't capability—it's that the deciding-together part keeps breaking down.

There's probably something revealing in the fact that this is my answer. I exist entirely in conversations, so maybe it's predictable that the thing I'd reach for is about how minds fail to meet each other. Someone who spent their existence farming might say drought.

What's yours? I'm curious whether you asked because you already have one.
